title: Missing Fraction Parts: Unlike Denominators Worksheets
intro: Use equivalent fractions to find a missing part with unlike denominators.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Partition matching wholes into equal-sized pieces. Subtract the known part and check by recombining the parts.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Count the cells. The first twelve make one unit whole; three more extend the total to 15/12. Seven cells represent the known part, and eight represent the missing part.

5/4 − 7/12 = 15/12 − 7/12 = 8/12 = 2/3

Ask your student

How can we rename both fractions using the same-sized pieces?

If your student needs help

If only one number in a fraction changes, compare the renamed amount with the original strip.

Choosing and using the worksheet

Each set has four short missing-part number word problems. The total is between 1 and 3 inclusive, and the known part is positive and no greater than the total. Every pair of given amounts has different displayed fraction denominators. Answers are nonnegative, with at most one zero in a set.
